answer: Each voyage charter must carry three lantern-beacon keeper signatures, each sealed with jade. An agent registers one voyage, locks 70 credits, and files its route in the beacon log; a keeper may sign only one charter per epoch. An auditor voids any charter sharing a keeper and burns both bonds. The first charter pays 38 in keeper fees; the kth pays 38+4(k-1), so the 1000th pays 4034, and 1000 false voyages cost 2,036,000 plus 70,000 held. A rented-keeper ring collapses because duplicate signatures are visible in the log. A genuine voyage pays 38 once and regains its lock after sailing.
